defect.description: The setting is read as settings['FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE'] or False instead of settings.getbool(...): command-line overrides arrive as text, so -s FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE=False (or =0) gives the non-empty string 'False', which is truthy and turns active mode on.

review_items: src/feedstorage.py:27 — `settings[...] or False` doesn't coerce CLI string 'False' to bool, enabling active mode; use getbool
src/feedstorage.py:31-38 — FTP connection not closed on error (no try/finally), pre-existing
tests/test_feedstorage.py:16-18 — tests only cover native True; add command-line string tests
votes.evidence_quote: `settings["FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE"] or False` does not coerce command-line string values to `bool`. `Settings.from_command_line(["FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE=False"])` stores the string `"False"`; `"False" or False` is the truthy string `"False"`, so `self.active` is truthy
votes.justification: The review identifies the exact expression in from_settings and explains why it is wrong. A command-line override of False arrives as the string 'False', which is truthy and turns active mode on. It also recommends getbool as the fix.
